title: Update incident response playbooks to reference error budgets + add budget exhaustion response procedures
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy
description:
Context
- As we roll out tier-aware SLOs + error budgets, we need oncall procedures to “feel” budget burn during incidents (and pre-incident) rather than treat budgets as an after-the-fact reporting artifact.
- This ticket updates incident response playbooks to explicitly incorporate: (a) error budget status checks, (b) burn-rate driven mitigations, and (c) the new policy behaviors when budgets are at risk/exhausted (change freezes, canary-only, overrides).

Goals
1) Add a canonical “Budget exhaustion response” runbook that oncall can follow during active burn spikes.
2) Update existing incident response playbooks/templates to reference error budget concepts (budget remaining, burn rate, scoped tier/service) and point to the policy.
3) Align responsibilities and comms triggers with Support/CS + status page guidance (Hosted vs Dedicated messaging).

In scope
- Confluence playbooks/runbooks (Oncall + Incident Response):
  - New runbook page: “Error budget exhaustion response” (checklist + mitigations + escalation)
  - Updates to existing incident response playbook pages to include budget checks as a standard step
  - Updates to postmortem template section: “Error budget impact” and “which controls would have triggered under policy”
- Oncall operationalization:
  - Ensure burn-rate alerts link to the new runbook and include the minimum annotations (tier/service/region + budget remaining)
  - Ensure incident-bot posts budget snapshots during active incidents (coordination w/ incident-bot PR already planned)

Out of scope
- Changing commercial SLAs / customer contract language
- Building new mitigation mechanisms (routing fallback, throttling, release gates are tracked in their own tickets); this ticket documents how/when to invoke them.

Deliverables
- Confluence pages (final links):
  - Runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/error-budget-exhaustion-response-runbook
  - Policy reference: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/error-budget-policy-and-enforcement
  - Comms guidance: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/error-budget-comms-guidelines
- Updated postmortem template section (Confluence): add required fields:
  - Tier(s) impacted
  - Budget remaining at incident start/end
  - Peak burn rate windows that paged
  - Mitigations executed (throttling / fallback routing / rollback / feature flags)
  - Enforcement impacts (gates blocked? overrides used?)

Acceptance criteria
- During an incident, oncall can answer within 10 minutes:
  - “Is budget burn the limiting factor right now (hosted/dedicated)?”
  - “What mitigation is recommended first for this tier and failure mode?”
  - “Are we in warn-only vs soft-block vs hard-block posture per policy?”
- Runbook is referenced from:
  - burn-rate alert annotations (ENG-2420)
  - incident-bot updates (incident-bot PR #52)
- Runbook explicitly separates Hosted vs Dedicated recommended actions and includes a decision tree for:
  - latency-only degradation vs 5xx spikes vs streaming disconnect spikes
  - Dedicated pool readiness dips vs API-level 5xx/latency
- Includes an “override / exception” section:
  - who can approve
  - TTL + required audit note
  - when overrides are prohibited (e.g., repeated regression causing burn)

Proposed runbook structure (MVP)
1) Triage & confirm budget context
   - Identify tier (Hosted/Dedicated) + service scope (gateway/routing/runtime/control-plane)
   - Open the SLO dashboard for the impacted scope (link panel)
   - Check budget remaining and burn rate windows (multi-window) for the last 1h/6h/3d
   - Confirm exclusions (customer-side timeouts, invalid auth, load test tenants) are not inflating
2) Decide response mode based on policy thresholds
   - Budget healthy: standard incident response; note budget context in channel
   - Budget at risk: require canary-only changes; prefer mitigations over feature rollouts
   - Budget exhausted: change freeze (except incident mitigation); gate overrides require approval + TTL
3) Mitigations by failure mode (tier-aware)
   - Hosted:
     - Enable protective throttling (if cascading failures / queue buildup)
     - Prefer routing failover + fallback model variants if error spikes
     - Reduce expensive routes/params (max tokens caps per policy, temporarily)
   - Dedicated:
     - Validate pool readiness and scheduler health
     - Avoid cross-customer mitigation that violates isolation guarantees
     - Prefer capacity actions: scale-up, re-balance within customer pool, suspend non-critical canaries
4) Comms & escalation
   - When to update status page vs Support/CS internal heads-up
   - Dedicated escalation path: dedicated-oncall + CSM liaison
   - Hosted escalation path: platform-oncall + incident commander
5) Recovery & follow-up
   - Confirm burn returns to normal; capture “budget burn story” in incident doc
   - Ensure policy actions applied/rolled back (freeze lifted, gates re-enabled)
   - Create follow-ups: instrumentation gaps, SLI misclassification, missing dashboards

Key collaborators / reviewers
- SRE policy: Sean Gallagher, Aisha Bello
- Change governance: Connor O’Brien
- Observability annotations: Sergio Costa
- Support/CS comms alignment: Dev Patel, Rachel Kim

Links / references

- Alerting standard: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/error-budget-burn-rate-alerting-standard
- SLO definitions: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/tiered-slo-definitions-hosted-vs-dedicated
- Related PRs:
  - incident-bot PR: sources/github/incident-bot/pull_request_52.json
  - docs updates: sources/github/redwood-docs/pull_request_312.json

Open questions
- Do we page on Dedicated pool readiness dips or ticket-only until we see false-positive rate? (proposed: page only if readiness dip correlates with customer-impact SLIs)
- For Hosted streaming: do we treat TTFT regression as budget-consuming the same way as disconnect spikes? (depends on final SLI weights; document current policy + revisit)

Implementation notes
- Keep the runbook strongly prescriptive (top 3 actions first) and avoid long background sections; incident time is not reading time.
- Add a short “Common pitfalls” section:
  - budget burn from SLI misclassification (e.g., 499/timeout handling)
  - per-region vs global confusion
  - Dedicated vs Hosted tier mis-tagging in metrics
